title: Device-independent quantification of steerability in tripartite scenario
authors: Xin-Hong Wang, Miao-Tzu Lin, Shin-Liang Chen
abstract: Quantum steering captures the ability of one party, through local measurements on a shared entangled state, to affect the conditional states held by distant parties in a way that admits no local explanation. Its device-independent (DI) quantification -- requiring no characterization of any state or measurement -- has been developed in the bipartite setting, notably through the framework of assemblage moment matrices (AMMs) [Phys. Rev. Lett. 116, 240401 (2016)], but has remained largely unexplored beyond it. Here, we extend the AMM framework to tripartite steering, covering both the scenario in which two parties jointly steer a third one (2-steer-1) and that in which a single party steers the remaining two (1-steer-2). For each scheme, we construct a semidefinite program that, from the observed correlations -- or merely from the violation of a Bell inequality -- yields lower bounds on the steering robustness of the underlying assemblage. As a by-product, our bounds also certify, in a DI manner, the incompatibility of the measurements performed by the steering parties.
summary: This work extends the concept of device-independent quantum steering quantification to three parties, analyzing two distinct tripartite scenarios. By employing the Assemblage Moment Matrices framework, the authors construct Semidefinite Programs to derive lower bounds on steering robustness. This provides a powerful, experimentally verifiable tool for certifying genuine multipartite nonlocality.
main_problem: The paper extends the device-independent (DI) quantification of quantum steering from the bipartite to the tripartite setting, analyzing two specific configurations: 2-steer-1 and 1-steer-2.
main_result: They develop Semidefinite Programs (SDPs) that yield lower bounds on the steering robustness for both tripartite scenarios, confirming the DI certification of measurement incompatibility.
method: The core method involves extending the Assemblage Moment Matrices (AMMs) framework to construct SDPs based on observed correlations or violations of Bell inequalities.
model_or_system: The analysis concerns a tripartite quantum state shared by three parties (Alice, Bob, Charlie) and quantifies the non-local correlations captured by quantum steering.
key_observables: Steering Robustness (SR), correlations $P(a, b, c|x, y, z)$, and violations of Bell inequalities like Mermin and Svetlichny.
important_parameters: The scenarios are defined by which parties are jointly steering which other parties (2-steer-1 vs. 1-steer-2).
main_assumptions: The quantification relies on the assumption that the observed correlations can be bounded by SDPs derived from the AMM framework, extending previous bipartite results.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the two tripartite steering scenarios: (a) 2-steer-1 (Alice and Bob steer Charlie) and (b) 1-steer-2 (Alice steers Bob and Charlie).
paper_structure: The paper systematically extends the AMM framework to the tripartite case, deriving SDPs for both 2-steer-1 and 1-steer-2, and establishing bounds on steering robustness by relating them to Bell inequality violations.
why_interesting: The rigorous, device-independent quantification of multipartite entanglement measures like steering is fundamental for certifying genuine multipartite quantum correlations in experimental settings.

The measurement devices of the steering parties are uncharacter- ized black boxes, which return an outcome for each input; the steered side is described by the conditional states. (a) The 2-steer-1 scenario: Alice and Bob, upon receiving the inputs x and y, return the outcomes a and b, and Charlie’s condi- tional states are steered to the assemblage {ρC ab|xy}a,b,x,y of Eq. (11). (b) The 1-steer-2 scenario: Alice, upon receiving the input x, returns the outcome a, and Bob and Charlie are jointly left with the assemblage {ρBC a|x}a,x of Eq. (20).
